nodes.content: Develop a learned turbulence closure that captures bidirectional energy transfer and remains stable across unseen coarse-graining scales.
requirements: Achieve below 10% energy-spectrum error against filtered direct numerical simulations at two unseen filter widths.
Maintain bounded kinetic energy and correct mean subgrid dissipation while reproducing intermittent backscatter.

nodes.content: Train a filter-width-conditioned equivariant stress network combining mean-dissipation-calibrated eddy viscosity with energy-budget-limited stochastic backscatter on filtered DNS.
Can a width-conditioned energy-budget cap preserve 95th-percentile backscatter bursts without destabilizing kinetic energy at unseen filter widths?
At unseen 16η and 32η, budget-capped backscatter keeps kinetic energy below 1.2× filtered-DNS levels and 95th-percentile backscatter error below 15%.
Train on 8η/24η filtered DNS; test 16η/32η LES for spectrum error, mean dissipation, 95th-percentile backscatter, and kinetic-energy bounds.
Run 20-turnover-time HIT-Re390 LES at 16η/32η, comparing capped and uncapped closures on spectra, mean dissipation, backscatter tails, and energy.
At 16η/32η, capped HIT-Re390 LES maintained ≤1.12× filtered-DNS energy and ≤11% backscatter P95 error; uncapped reached 1.43×.
Select capped backscatter over uncapped: it held kinetic energy within 12% of filtered DNS while preserving backscatter tails.
Benchmark the selected capped closure against filtered HIT-Re390 DNS at 16η/32η, requiring <10% spectral error and <5% mean-dissipation bias.
Run three-seed capped-closure LES at 16η/32η and measure shell-integrated spectrum error and mean SGS dissipation bias against filtered HIT-Re390 DNS.
HIT-Re390 validation report: three-seed 16η/32η spectrum errors of 7.4%/8.7% and mean SGS dissipation biases of 2.9%/4.1%.
Audit the HIT-Re390 validation report against archived three-seed trajectories, independently recomputing spectral errors, dissipation biases, and confidence intervals.
Independent three-seed audit confirmed 16η/32η spectral errors of 7.4%/8.7% (95% CI upper bounds 8.6%/9.6%) and dissipation biases of 2.9%/4.1%.
Replacing instantaneous clipping with an SGS-energy reservoir keeps 99th-percentile backscatter error below 15% and kinetic energy below 1.2× DNS.
Run paired 20-turnover HIT-Re390 LES at 16η/32η, comparing reservoir-funded and clipped backscatter by P99 error and peak energy.
Reservoir-funded 16η/32η LES had P99 backscatter errors of 19%/24% and peak energies of 1.18×/1.27× filtered DNS, exceeding proposed thresholds.
Extend paired reservoir-versus-clipping HIT-Re390 LES at 32η to 40 turnover times across five seeds; remeasure P99 backscatter and peak energy.
Across five new 40-turnover 32η reservoir runs, P99 backscatter error was 13% and full-trajectory peak energy stayed ≤1.18× DNS.
Do forcing seeds explain conflicting 32η reservoir P99 errors (24% versus 13%) and peak-energy ratios (1.27× versus 1.18×)?
Reanalyze both 32η cohorts over identical 20-turnover windows with common DNS normalization; rerun matched forcing seeds to isolate seed effects.
Train a scale-equivariant wavelet-flux closure with signed local transfers, mean-dissipation calibration, and an enforced resolved-energy inequality.
Fit wavelet-flux closure on 8η/24η filtered HIT-Re390 DNS, enforce a discrete energy inequality, then test 16η/32η spectra, dissipation, and backscatter.
Train WaveFlux-v1 on 8η/24η HIT-Re390 snapshots with signed-flux loss and energy projection; run 16η/32η LES.
WaveFlux-v1 benchmark bundle contains trained weights, energy-projection settings, and 16η/32η LES spectra, SGS-dissipation, backscatter, and kinetic-energy traces.
Audit WaveFlux-v1 bundle against filtered HIT-Re390 DNS at 16η/32η for spectral error, dissipation bias, backscatter P95, and energy.
WaveFlux-v1 at 16η/32η achieved 6.8%/7.9% spectral error, 2.5%/3.4% dissipation bias, 9%/12% backscatter-P95 error, and ≤1.11× DNS peak energy.
Use a width-conditioned neural potential that predicts signed SGS flux while enforcing a discrete kinetic-energy bound through convex projection.
Does convex energy projection suppress P99 backscatter at unseen 32η when the neural potential approaches its kinetic-energy bound?
At 32η, projection keeps P99 backscatter error below 15% during timesteps when unprojected kinetic energy exceeds 95% of its bound.
Run paired 32η HIT-Re390 LES; compare projected versus unprojected P99 backscatter against DNS when preprojection kinetic energy exceeds 95% bound.
At 32η with preprojection energy >95% of bound, projected P99 backscatter error reached 28% versus 12% unprojected.
Replay five 32η forcing seeds, comparing projected versus unprojected DNS-referenced backscatter P99 errors when preprojection energy exceeds 95% of bound.
Across five additional 32η seeds, projected near-bound P99 backscatter error averaged 13% (10–14% by seed), versus 19% unprojected.
Are the conflicting 32η projected P99 errors (28% versus 10–14%) driven by forcing-seed variability or near-bound sample scarcity?
Recompute both 32η cohorts with identical DNS normalization; stratify near-bound P99 errors by seed and event count using bootstrap intervals.
Recompute six-seed 32η near-bound P99 errors under common DNS normalization; bootstrap per-seed errors against qualifying-event counts.
32η near-bound audit notebook contains six-seed P99 errors, qualifying-event counts, and bootstrap 95% intervals under common DNS normalization.
Fit a filter-conditioned Mori–Zwanzig memory closure with calibrated mean dissipation and Lyapunov-bounded stochastic forcing for intermittent backscatter.
What filter-scaled memory horizon preserves backscatter bursts at unseen 16η/32η while maintaining negative Lyapunov drift?
A 0.5Δ/uΔ memory horizon yields <15% backscatter-P95 error and negative quadratic-Lyapunov drift above 1.1× DNS energy at 16η/32η.
Fit memory kernels on 8η/24η DNS; compare 0.25, 0.5, and 1 Δ/uΔ horizons at 16η/32η for backscatter-P95 and Lyapunov drift.
Run three-seed HIT-Re390 LES at 16η/32η for all three memory horizons; measure backscatter-P95 error and energy-conditioned quadratic-Lyapunov drift.
At 0.5Δ/uΔ, 16η/32η backscatter-P95 errors were 10%/12%, with negative quadratic-Lyapunov drift above 1.1× DNS energy.
Repeat 0.5Δ/uΔ HIT-Re390 LES with five held-out forcing seeds at 16η/32η; bootstrap backscatter-P95 errors and drift above 1.1× DNS energy.
Across five held-out seeds, 32η backscatter-P95 error reached 21%, and quadratic-Lyapunov drift above 1.1× DNS energy turned positive.
Which forcing-seed regimes make the 0.5Δ/uΔ memory kernel lose negative high-energy drift at 32η despite earlier three-seed stability?
At 32η, seeds with forcing-power CV>0.3 destabilize 0.5Δ/uΔ memory; shortening to 0.25Δ/uΔ restores negative high-energy drift.
Pool original and held-out 32η seeds; stratify forcing-power CV at 0.3, rerun high-CV seeds at 0.25Δ/uΔ, compare drift and P95.
Stratify eight 32η seeds at forcing-power CV 0.3; compare 0.5Δ/uΔ drift/P95 and rerun high-CV seeds at 0.25Δ/uΔ.
At 32η, high-CV seeds showed 12% P95 error and negative high-energy drift at 0.5Δ/uΔ; shortening memory raised error to 19%.
After high-CV stability, stratify remaining 32η seeds by forcing autocorrelation and high-energy episode counts; reassess 0.5Δ/uΔ drift.
Compute forcing autocorrelation and high-energy episode counts for eight 32η seeds; compare 0.5 versus 0.25Δ/uΔ drift by CV stratum.
In CV>0.3 32η seeds, persistent-forcing episodes had positive 0.5Δ/uΔ drift; 0.25Δ/uΔ restored negative episode-wise drift.
Choose 0.5Δ/uΔ by default for lower P95 error; shorten to 0.25Δ/uΔ during persistent high-CV forcing to restore negative drift.
Implement persistent-forcing CV>0.3 switching from 0.5 to 0.25Δ/uΔ; test 16η/32η spectra, mean SGS dissipation, backscatter-P95, and energy bounds.
Run five-seed 16η/32η HIT-Re390 LES, switching memory after forcing-power CV>0.3 persists one turnover; measure spectra, dissipation, backscatter-P95, energy.
AdaptiveMemory-v1 benchmark bundle contains five-seed 16η/32η trajectories, switching logs, spectra, SGS dissipation, backscatter-P95, and kinetic-energy traces.
Audit AdaptiveMemory-v1’s five-seed 16η/32η bundle against filtered DNS for spectral error, dissipation bias, backscatter-P95, and peak kinetic energy.
AdaptiveMemory-v1 at 16η/32η achieved 8.1%/9.2% spectral error, 3.1%/4.3% dissipation bias, 11%/13% backscatter-P95 error, and ≤1.15× DNS peak energy.
